newsitem.title: UK: Willis Corroon says to wind up Sovereign.
newsitem.headline: Willis Corroon says to wind up Sovereign.

text.p: British insurance broker Willis Corroon Group Plc said on Friday it had decided to wind up its Sovereign Marine & General Insurance subsidiary.
The decision follows an unexpectedly adverse outcome of the arbitration of a dispute with a reinsurer of two of Sovereign's casualty surplus treaties.
Willis said provisional liquidators had been appointed to Sovereign which ceased underwriting and was placed into run-off during 1991.
Willis chairman John Reeve said the decision had been taken with regret but that it was in the best interests of shareholders.

"We have already committed substantial group resources to maintaining Sovereign's solvency since the company went into run-off in 1991; the board cannot justify a continuation of this commitment," said Reeve.

The company said the award by the arbitrator had meant adjustment to the disputed treaties had substantially increased Sovereign's liabilities and would require additional finacial resources if Sovereign were not liquidated.
Sovereign's underwriting reserves were strengthened significantly in 1991 and 1992, resulting in underwriting losses of 58 million stg being charged against the group's results for those years.
Further underwriting losses totalling 14.8 million stg were similarly charged in the subsequent four years.
